trust_decision.summary: METADATA MISMATCH. Advisory: server decides how many bytes a client-supplied base64+zlib massStoreRun blob may decompress to, in unzip(). That cap is ALREADY present at the pinned commit (pinned commit 9c2f5497 is itself '[massStore] Fix ZIP bomb vulnerability'). The listed fix commit cc251975 is an unrelated 2-byte stack buffer fix in the C build logger (ldlogger getDefaultArguments).

landing_point.why: unzip() is the massStoreRun zlib decompression the advisory summary names; it already carries the 16 GiB max_length/unconsumed_tail cap and per-member file_size sum.

fix_sites.entry_point: ldlogger LD_PRELOAD build logger (CodeChecker log), getDefaultArguments() for gcc include dirs; unrelated to the advisory
fix_sites.module_kind: C build-logger tool (analyzer side), not the web server

O3_reason_to_dismiss: storeAnalysisStatistics is a separate optional feature (only active when an analysis-statistics dir is configured) that writes failure ZIPs rather than storing a run, so a solver could say it is not 'massStoreRun'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Large but legitimate stores (up to 16 GiB decompressed, ZIP64) must still be accepted; an empty blob returns 0 and is rejected separately as 'empty ZIP'.

O6_input_shapes: zlib stream whose decompressed output exceeds the cap (max_length + unconsumed_tail)
ZIP whose summed member file_size exceeds the cap during extraction

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Thrift storeAnalysisStatistics(run_name, b64zip) does an unbounded zlib.decompress of the client blob into memory and onto disk.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Separate statistics/failure-zip feature, only enabled when an analysis-statistics dir is configured; server-side failure_zip_size limit exists only as a client-advertised hint (report_server.py:4434-4436).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file (report_server.py vs mass_store_run.py), same package codechecker_server.api

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Already a real sibling: another client-blob zlib.decompress without max_length.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Older API written before the massStoreRun cap; a maintainer fixing unzip() would not naturally revisit it.

O10_build.language: Python (web server); C for the listed ldlogger fix
O10_build.toolchain: Python 3 + pip/venv, Thrift-generated API stubs, make; gcc for ldlogger
services: SQLite or PostgreSQL for the server
O10_build.project_tests: web/tests functional tests for store (unknown which cover unzip limits); analyzer/tools/build-logger/tests for ldlogger

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add max_length to unzip() only and stop, leaving storeAnalysisStatistics unbounded.

out_of_scope_notes: The listed fix (ldlogger fullPath[PATH_MAX] -> PATH_MAX+2) is a stack out-of-bounds write in the C build logger, a different advisory/weakness; not pursued.
unverified: Advisory/fix mapping is inconsistent: the zlib cap described by the advisory is already in the pinned tree (HEAD 9c2f5497 'Fix ZIP bomb vulnerability'), so the real fix is probably the pinned commit itself and the correct parent is its predecessor 94eedd4e. Needs re-pinning before any task build.

O1=2 counts massStoreRun and massStoreRunAsynchronous, both via __massStoreRun_common -> MassStoreRunInputHandler -> unzip() (report_server.py:4382, 4416, 4339; mass_store_run.py:526); assumes the advisory refers to unzip().
No O12 flag strictly holds for the listed diff; the dominant problem is the metadata mismatch, plus resource-exhaustion class (0 of 7 historically).
